messages:
anya: Heads-up — saw a parse_repair spike on the hosted canary this morning, correlated with a p95 token latency jump. dashboard: https://dash.redwood.local/d/parse/repair-history :eyes:

matt: Seen that too, looks like repair attempts per-invoke spiked from ~0.2 to ~1.8 on the int8 canary after the new prompt tweak.

anya: exact numbers from sampling run: parse_failure_rate went 0.7% -> 3.5%, repair_attempts_per_invoke 0.25 -> 1.9, p95 tokens +120ms.

cheng: current defaults are repair_quota=5, initial_backoff_ms=50, max_backoff_ms=400. that 5 is generous for noisy models — it can amplify load.

sam: do we have data on repair success vs harm? like how often repair yields a valid JSON vs it just triggers another full invoke?

anya: quick eval: out of 1000 failures, repairs returned valid JSON 38% of time, but 14% resulted in partial/garbled tokens that still required another repair -> extra token cost.

lina: SLA concern: repair storms are pushing some routes over our p95 SLO. We need a per-invoke budget + route-level circuit breaker.

cheng: proposal: tighten defaults for canary tiers: repair_quota=1, initial_backoff_ms=200, backoff_multiplier=2, max_attempts=2. and add a per-route repair_rate_limit (e.g., 5 rps) so a noisy route can't flood retry subsystem.

matt: agree. Also want to track new metrics: repair_success_rate, repairs_per_invoke, repair_cost_tokens, p95_tokens_after_repair. add them to the model-onboard dashboard.

anya: suggested quick experiment: A/B 10% traffic -> new config (quota=1, init_backoff=200, max_attempts=2) vs baseline for 24h. collect the above metrics + end-to-end function success rate.

sam: will run offline eval too — run the same prompt set under quantized and fp16 variants to see delta in parse failure vs repair benefit.

lina: we should also define SLA-safe fallback: if repairs exceed budget or reach circuit-breaker, return a structured error payload to the app (HTTP 422 with "structured_output_unavailable" and non-retryable flag) so clients don't retry blindly.

cheng: config snippet for canary (will push as feature flag):

```yaml
repairs:
  repair_quota: 1
  initial_backoff_ms: 200
  backoff_multiplier: 2
  max_attempts: 2
  per_route_rate_limit_rps: 5
  circuit_breaker:
    window_s: 60
    failure_threshold_pct: 5
    cooldown_s: 300
```

matt: nice. I'll add dashboard tiles and an alert rule: if repairs_per_invoke > 0.8 and p95_tokens increased by >50ms then notify #eng-oncall.

deploy-bot: Alert: hosted-canary/parse-repair configured for staged rollout (10%). See deploy link: https://deploy.redwood.local/rollouts/6155554321

anya: assignment: @cheng implement canary feature-flag + config; @matt add metrics + alerts; @sam run offline eval on quant variants; @lina write short SLO-safe fallback doc. aim to have A/B live by EOD tomorrow.

sam: quick Q — for offline eval, what's the golden prompt set? use the 12k_struct_output_set v3?

anya: yep, use 12k_struct_output_set_v3 plus the new user-submitted set from last week's dogfood (folder: s3://evals/struct-dogfood/).

lina: also include a tiny latency cost sim: estimate extra tokens from repair attempts -> translate to $/1000 calls. want to show cost delta in the runbook.

cheng: will instrument and flip the FF for 10% now. pushing change to edge with canary tag.

matt: dashboards wired, alert ready. sending invite for a 30-min sync tomorrow to review A/B results.

anya: thanks — will monitor. if we see repair_success_rate drop <30% or p95 cost increases, we rollback. :thumbsup:

lina: documenting decision in runbook after sync. :spiral_note_pad:

anya: closing loop for now, will post summary after 24h.

matt: :rocket:
